My favorite relevant experiment is the delayed choice quantum eraser which will probably require some serious reading to wrap your head around but once again a TL/DR: The decision to measure something in the future, can change how it behaves in the present. Scientists shoot photons at a pair of slits to see if the photons are waves or if they are particles, and then after the photons have been fully absorbed and recorded they either check which path it took, or they don't check. In all of the cases where they do check which path the thing took, they find that that thing had behaved as if it were a particle, and in the cases where they don't check they find that it had behaved like a wave, even though the decision of checking or not checking was made long after the photon was emitted and absorbed.
